newsitem.title: FINLAND: Belgian PM wants EMU framework fixed at Amsterdam.
newsitem.headline: Belgian PM wants EMU framework fixed at Amsterdam.

text.p: Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene said on Wednesday that the whole legal framework for European economic and monetary union (EMU) should be fixed at the June 16-17 summit of European Union leaders in Amsterdam.

"The whole legal framework of monetary union should be fixed, if possible, at Amsterdam," Dehaene said at a news conference here after meeting Finnish President Martti Ahtisaari and Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen.

Dehaene said Belgium and Finland were prepared to support the introduction of a new text as an addition to the Maastricht treaty's article 103, which envisages coordination of EU member countries' economic policies.
Referring to the EMU budget stability pact intended to enforce fiscal discipline once the single currency has been launched in 1999, Dehaene said:

"When you have a specification about how the (EMU convergence) criteria have to go further after the start of monetary union, it is also logical to say how the coordination of economic policies will be organised."
But any new protocol to article 103 should be agreed speedily.
"We should have approval of the stability pact very fast, but we are open to have a second text giving more operational effect to article 103," he said.
"That is something which is in line with the treaty but it should happen fast," he said, adding he did not expect this to be a major difficulty.

"I don't think there is a big difficulty, the only problem is to have that (new text) concrete and have it concrete on time so that you do not create a period of uncertainty," he said, adding: "We don't want to touch the stability pact as such."

The new socialist government in France on Monday said it needed more time to review the stability pact, raising doubts whether EU leaders would be able to approve wide-ranging reforms in a revised treaty designed to prepare the 15-member bloc for its ambitious expansion eastward.
